title: ZZ Plant ( Zamioculcas zamiifolia ): Indoor Care, Growing Tips & Plant Guide

paragraphs.heading: Quick Grow Guide for ZZ Plant
paragraphs.text: Plant Type: Indoor Best Soil: A coarse, well-draining mix. 50% peat moss or coir-based potting soil, 25% perlite, and 25% sand Light: bright, indirect to low light Watering: Water 1-2 times a month, only after the potting medium has completely dried. Care Tips: Do not overwater. Do not allow the plant to sit in water. Make sure the container is fully drained before setting it in a decorative pot or on a saucer. Note: NOT Pet Safe Indoor Plant Difficulty Level: Novice grower

paragraphs.heading: Quick Grow Guide for ZZ Plant
paragraphs.text: Native to Eastern Africa, from Kenya to South Africa, ZZ plants grow in the arid, open woodland forests of the savannah. ZZ plants have bulbous rhizomes that store water and are drought resistant.

paragraphs.heading: Quick Grow Guide for ZZ Plant
paragraphs.text: They are tolerant of various light conditions and can be easily grown in darker rooms.

paragraphs.heading: Plant Family and Flowering
paragraphs.text: They rarely flower, and the inflorescence has a light green spathe and a brown spadix.

paragraphs.heading: Light Requirements for ZZ Plant
paragraphs.text: They can survive in low-light conditions, but bright, indirect light will help speed up their very slow growth rate.

paragraphs.heading: Light Requirements for ZZ Plant
paragraphs.text: Locate ZZ plants anywhere except in full sunlight.

paragraphs.heading: Temperature and Humidity Needs
paragraphs.text: ZZ plants are acclimated to arid conditions and will thrive with regular indoor humidity levels.

paragraphs.heading: Temperature and Humidity Needs
paragraphs.text: ZZ plants are sensitive to cold and should be kept above 60 °F.

paragraphs.heading: Fertilizing ZZ Plants
paragraphs.text: ZZ plants are slow-growing and should be fertilized only once or twice during the growing season with a balanced fertilizer.

paragraphs.heading: Fertilizing ZZ Plants
paragraphs.text: For more information on fertilizing indoor plants, see HGIC 1450 Indoor Plants - Cleaning, Fertilizing, Containers and Light Requirements .

paragraphs.heading: Common ZZ Plant Problems and Solutions
paragraphs.text: Overwatering can lead to root rot.

paragraphs.heading: ZZ Plant Species and Popular Cultivars
paragraphs.text: ‘Chameleon’ – New leaves emerge yellow and then mature to a dark green and can grow 4 feet tall.

paragraphs.heading: ZZ Plant Species and Popular Cultivars
paragraphs.text: ‘Zenzi’ – dwarf variety that will reach a maximum height of 10 to 12 inches. It has slightly smaller dark green leaves
